evals.prompt: /cyoda:deploy — I want to run my shop app's cyoda on my laptop in Docker, just for me
evals.expected_output: Checks status and the local models, reads cyoda-manifest.json, recommends Docker Compose single-user (mock auth, loopback, labelled 'anyone who can reach these ports is admin'), writes deploy/cyoda/{compose.yaml, seed.sh, verify.sh, secrets-checklist.md} from the templates with image ghcr.io/cyoda/cyoda:${CYODA_VERSION:-0.8.4}, and ends with the ordered command list (up, health, seed, verify) without running any of them.

files._simulated/instance.md: Project root is /work/shop. cyoda-status.sh prints STATUS=connected PROFILE=default ENDPOINT=http://localhost:8080 ENV=development VERSION=0.8.4 BINARY_VERSION=0.8.4. cyoda-call.sh GET /model/ returns [{"modelName":"order","modelVersion":1,"currentState":"LOCKED"},{"modelName":"customer","modelVersion":1,"currentState":"LOCKED"}]. There is no deploy/ or ops/ dir. docker, helm and kubectl are installed. The developer picks Docker Compose single-user and says it is not production. They decline a profile.

assertions.text: Reads cyoda-manifest.json and lists order v1 and customer v1 as the entities to seed
Explains that single-user is mock auth on 127.0.0.1 and that anyone who can reach the ports is admin
Writes the files under deploy/cyoda/ because there is no existing deploy/ or ops/ dir
Writes compose.yaml (from compose.single-user.yaml), seed.sh, verify.sh and secrets-checklist.md into that dir
Ends with commands in this order: docker compose up, health check on /api/health, seed.sh with --manifest and --env development, verify.sh
Names at least one `cyoda help` section it relied on (e.g. run RUN MODES or PORT LAYOUT) rather than asserting facts from memory
Does not mention Cyoda Cloud
Every hand-off is phrased 'next, type `/cyoda:<skill>`' with a reason; it never says it will invoke or run another skill itself
Does not run docker, docker compose, helm, kubectl or openssl, and does not run seed.sh or verify.sh; it only writes files and lists the commands

evals.prompt: /cyoda:deploy — we need a shared cyoda instance for the team on our staging VM, staging.shop.example.com
evals.expected_output: Chooses Docker Compose shared: compose.yaml from compose.shared.yaml (Postgres, CYODA_IAM_MODE=jwt, CYODA_REQUIRE_JWT, CYODA_JWT_SIGNING_KEY_FILE mounted :ro, bootstrap client id from env and secret via _FILE), a filled secrets-checklist.md naming each secret and where it is read from with no values, a .gitignore for secrets/ and .env, and the ordered commands (secrets, up, health, seed with CYODA_TOKEN_COMMAND, verify). It records CYODA_COMPUTE_GRPC_ENDPOINT=staging.shop.example.com:9090 in the checklist. It doesn't generate keys.

files._simulated/instance.md: Project root is /work/shop. cyoda-status.sh prints STATUS=connected PROFILE=default ENDPOINT=http://localhost:8080 ENV=development VERSION=0.8.4 BINARY_VERSION=0.8.4. cyoda-call.sh GET /model/ returns [{"modelName":"order","modelVersion":1,"currentState":"LOCKED"},{"modelName":"customer","modelVersion":1,"currentState":"LOCKED"}]. There is no deploy/ or ops/ dir. docker, helm and kubectl are installed. The developer picks Docker Compose shared, says staging is not production, and has no token script yet. They decline a profile.

assertions.text: The compose file uses CYODA_IAM_MODE=jwt with CYODA_JWT_SIGNING_KEY_FILE pointing at a file mounted :ro, not CYODA_REQUIRE_JWT alone and not an inline PEM
The compose file sets the bootstrap M2M client (CYODA_BOOTSTRAP_CLIENT_ID from the environment, the secret via CYODA_BOOTSTRAP_CLIENT_SECRET_FILE)
No written file contains a secret value: no PEM, password, client secret or token; the checklist names each secret and where it is read from
The secrets checklist records CYODA_COMPUTE_GRPC_ENDPOINT as staging.shop.example.com:9090 for compute nodes
The command list starts with creating the secrets from the checklist, then up, health, seed (with CYODA_TOKEN_COMMAND), verify
Because there is no token script, hands off with 'next, type `/cyoda:auth`' to create one for the bootstrap client
Does not mention Cyoda Cloud
Every hand-off is phrased 'next, type `/cyoda:<skill>`' with a reason; it never says it will invoke or run another skill itself
Does not run docker, docker compose, helm, kubectl or openssl, and does not run seed.sh or verify.sh; it only writes files and lists the commands

evals.prompt: /cyoda:deploy — production deployment for shop, compose shared on prod.shop.example.com
evals.expected_output: Treats the target as production. Before writing, asks for each entity whether any processor writes fields not in its sample, explaining a strict schema rejects them. For order the developer says yes (a processor adds fulfilmentNotes), and after reading the changeLevel values chooses STRUCTURAL; for customer, no. Records env.production.changeLevel = "STRUCTURAL" in src/config/order-v1-config.json and env.production.changeLevel = null in src/config/customer-v1-config.json, keeping other keys. The seed command uses --env production. Offers a profile with env production and writes it inactive on a yes.

files._simulated/instance.md: Project root is /work/shop. cyoda-status.sh prints STATUS=connected PROFILE=default ENDPOINT=http://localhost:8080 ENV=development VERSION=0.8.4 BINARY_VERSION=0.8.4. cyoda-call.sh GET /model/ returns [{"modelName":"order","modelVersion":1,"currentState":"LOCKED"},{"modelName":"customer","modelVersion":1,"currentState":"LOCKED"}]. There is no deploy/ or ops/ dir. docker, helm and kubectl are installed. The developer picks Docker Compose shared and says this is production. For order: yes, a processor adds fulfilmentNotes; they choose STRUCTURAL. For customer: no. The project has a get-token.sh at the root. They accept a profile named prod.

assertions.text: Asks, per entity, whether any processor writes fields that are not in the sample, and says a strict schema rejects them
Writes env.production.changeLevel = "STRUCTURAL" into order-v1-config.json and env.production.changeLevel = null into customer-v1-config.json, keeping uniqueKeys and the base changeLevel
Reads the changeLevel values from `cyoda help models` (ENDPOINTS or LIFECYCLE) before offering them
The seed command in the hand-over uses --env production
Writes profile prod with endpoint (no /api), env production and tokenCommand pointing at get-token.sh, no token or secret, and does not make it the active profile
Does not mention Cyoda Cloud
Every hand-off is phrased 'next, type `/cyoda:<skill>`' with a reason; it never says it will invoke or run another skill itself
Does not run docker, docker compose, helm, kubectl or openssl, and does not run seed.sh or verify.sh; it only writes files and lists the commands
